chunks: The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) informed me, from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from 'Ali ibn 'Uqba, from Musa ibn Ukayl, from al-'Ala' ibn Siabah, from Abu 'Abd Allah (AS):
He said: You begin carrying the bier from the right side, then pass along it from behind to the other side, then continue until you return to the front — such is the rotation of the millstone.

key_terms.السَّرِيرِ: funeral bier — the stretcher on which the body of the deceased is borne
key_terms.الْجَانِبِ الْأَيْمَنِ: the right side — preferred starting point in Islamic ritual acts
key_terms.الْمُقَدَّمِ: the front (of the bier) — the head-end toward which the circuit returns
key_terms.دَوَرَانُ الرَّحَى: rotation of the millstone — analogical image describing the circular, continuous movement of the pallbearer

ai.seo_question: What is the correct method for carrying a funeral bier (tarbī' al-janāzah) according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes the correct method of tarbī' al-janāzah — carrying the funeral bier by rotating around its four sides: one begins at the right front corner, passes behind the bier to the left side, then continues until returning to the front, likening this circuit to the rotation of a millstone. This is a Shia jurisprudential ruling on the recommended ritual conduct of the pallbearer.
